text_blocks.snippet: The Archdiocese of Los Angeles operates the largest Catholic school system in the United States, with more than 245 schools across Los Angeles, Ventura, and Santa Barbara counties.
snippet_highlighted_words: more than 245 schools across Los Angeles, Ventura, and Santa Barbara counties

list.snippet: Elementary & Preschool: Serves around 43,000 students from Transitional Kindergarten (TK) through 8th grade. Programs feature specialized options like STEM networks, microschools, and dual language immersion (such as English-Spanish and English-Mandarin).

High Schools: Includes over 50 Catholic high schools spanning archdiocesan, parish-run, and private/independent formats. Well-known examples include Loyola High School (boys) and Immaculate Heart High School (girls) in the central LA area.
Elementary: Rolling admissions are common for preschool, TK, and elementary grades year-round if space allows.
High School: Applications are typically due in January with decisions released in February.

text_blocks.snippet: You can look up specific neighborhood campuses through the official LA Catholic Schools Locator tool.
